system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Shanghai, China. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Shanghai itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Shanghai space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (West Bund/Xuhui, M50/Moganshan Road, The Bund/Rockbund, Jing'an, Former French Concession, Putuo, Pudong) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Shanghai spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Shanghai, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: ShanghART Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1996 by Lorenz Helbling, the pioneering Chinese contemporary gallery; represents Zhang Enli, Ding Yi, Yang Fudong, Geng Jianyi, Xu Zhen and Liang Shaoji, with Beijing and Singapore spaces and a constant presence at Basel and Frieze.

galleries.name: Antenna Space
galleries.note: Simon Wang's gallery is the key launchpad for a younger international generation — Guan Xiao, Li Ming, Yu Honglei, Cui Jie — and among the most critically watched Chinese galleries at Basel, Frieze and biennials.

galleries.name: BANK / MABSOCIETY
galleries.note: Mathieu Borysevicz's curator-led gallery, known for sharp, research-driven exhibitions and for rediscovering overlooked Chinese artists alongside international emerging names.

galleries.name: Perrotin Shanghai
galleries.note: The French mega-gallery's mainland flagship; blue-chip international programme (Murakami, JR, Kusama, Sophie Calle) that helped make the Huqiu Road building the Bund's gallery hub.

galleries.name: Lisson Gallery Shanghai
galleries.note: London gallery's mainland outpost, bringing Ai Weiwei, Anish Kapoor, Carmen Herrera and Marina Abramović-calibre programming to Shanghai audiences.

galleries.name: Don Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 2008 by Cynthia Wang; a consistently rigorous programme of Chinese conceptual and painting practices (Chen Wei, Ma Qiusha, Li Shan, Tang Dixin) with strong fair and institutional traction.

galleries.name: MadeIn Gallery
galleries.note: Xu Zhen's artist-founded gallery, an incubator for experimental Chinese practices and a platform that blurs corporate, curatorial and artistic production.

galleries.name: Massimo De Carlo Shanghai
galleries.note: Milan gallery's Shanghai space, showing Maurizio Cattelan, Rudolf Stingel, Yan Pei-Ming and younger internationals in a landmark Bund heritage building.

galleries.name: AIKE
galleries.note: Formerly Aike-Dellarco; a serious cross-cultural programme pairing Chinese abstraction and conceptual art with Italian and international figures, long-standing at Art Basel Hong Kong.

galleries.name: Capsule Shanghai
galleries.note: Enrico Polato's garden-lane gallery is one of the city's best barometers of emerging Asian art, with a growing international fair profile and a Venice outpost.

galleries.name: Vanguard Gallery
galleries.note: Lise Li's gallery, founded 2004 at M50; early champion of Chinese video, photography and installation (Chen Zhe, Liu Chuang, Hu Weiyi).

galleries.name: Almine Rech Shanghai
galleries.note: Global gallery's Shanghai space (opened 2022), presenting its roster of international painters and postwar estates to mainland collectors.

galleries.name: Gallery Vacancy
galleries.note: Young, internationally minded gallery with a tightly curated roster of emerging painters and sculptors; a regular at Frieze, Basel Hong Kong and Liste-type platforms.

galleries.name: Pearl Lam Galleries
galleries.note: Long-running Hong Kong–Shanghai operation mixing Chinese abstraction, international contemporary art and design; a fixture of the city's collecting scene.

galleries.name: LINSEED
galleries.note: Founded 2021, one of the most talked-about young Shanghai galleries, showing emerging Chinese and diasporic artists and quickly building a fair and institutional profile.

galleries.name: Ota Fine Arts Shanghai
galleries.note: Tokyo/Singapore gallery's West Bund space; brings Yayoi Kusama, Tomoko Kashiki and pan-Asian conceptual practices into dialogue with Chinese artists.

galleries.name: Shanghai Gallery of Art
galleries.address_hint: Three on the Bund, 3 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road
galleries.note: Opened 2004 in the Three on the Bund building; an early exhibition-driven space that hosted major curated shows and remains a Bund landmark for contemporary art.

galleries.name: Leo Gallery
galleries.note: Established Shanghai–Hong Kong gallery with a broad Chinese and international programme and one of the most visited addresses in the Concession.

galleries.name: Chronus Art Center (CAC)
galleries.note: China's leading nonprofit dedicated to media art — research, residencies and exhibitions on art, technology and computation.

galleries.name: OCAT Shanghai
galleries.note: Shanghai node of the OCAT network, focused on media art, curatorial research and exhibitions supporting experimental Chinese practices.

galleries.name: Eastlink Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1999 by Li Liang, one of Shanghai's oldest private galleries and an early supporter of edgy performance and installation art in the city.

galleries.name: Shanghai Center of Photography (SCôP)
galleries.note: Founded by Liu Heung Shing; the city's dedicated nonprofit photography exhibition space, anchoring the West Bund cluster.

galleries.name: Qiao Space
galleries.note: Collector Qiao Zhibing's exhibition space, which staged ambitious curated shows and helped seed the West Bund art district before TANK Shanghai.

galleries.name: Longlati Foundation
galleries.note: Collection-based nonprofit with a research and exhibition programme focused on women artists and emerging contemporary practices.

galleries.name: Hive Contemporary Art Center, Shanghai
galleries.note: Shanghai space of the influential Beijing gallery, known for a strong painting programme and consistent art-fair presence.

galleries.name: A+ Contemporary (Asia Contemporary Art Space)
galleries.note: Taipei-linked space at M50 promoting young Asian artists through exhibitions, prizes and cross-strait exchange projects.

galleries.name: Aura Gallery
galleries.note: Long-established gallery with Taipei roots, historically important for photography and contemporary Chinese art at M50.

galleries.name: OFOTO Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 2005, a specialist photography and image-based gallery that has shaped the reception of Chinese contemporary photography.

galleries.name: m97 Gallery
galleries.note: Shanghai's best-known dedicated photography dealer since 2006, showing Chinese and international photographers and vintage material.

galleries.name: Danysz Gallery Shanghai
galleries.note: Magda Danysz's Shanghai space, notable for urban/street art, Obey- and JR-adjacent figures and large-scale mural projects in the city.

galleries.name: Art Labor Gallery
galleries.note: Independent gallery with a long record of showing emerging Chinese and expatriate artists in the Concession.

galleries.name: Asia Art Center Shanghai
galleries.note: Taipei-founded gallery's Shanghai branch, presenting modern Chinese masters alongside contemporary abstraction and sculpture.

galleries.name: Art+ Shanghai Gallery
galleries.note: Bund-side gallery with a bilingual programme championing mid-career and emerging Chinese artists and ink-adjacent practices.

galleries.name: island6 Arts Center
galleries.note: Artist collective (Liu Dao) and nonprofit space producing LED and new-media works; a long-standing fixture of the M50 scene.

galleries.name: M Art Center
galleries.note: Veteran M50 gallery showing established and mid-career Chinese painters and photographers.

galleries.name: Yibo Gallery
galleries.note: Long-running M50 gallery with a focus on contemporary Chinese painting and abstraction.

galleries.name: AroundSpace Gallery
galleries.note: Bund-area gallery presenting emerging Chinese and Japanese artists, with an emphasis on drawing, painting and small-scale works.

galleries.name: MAO Space
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery known for concept-led solo presentations by younger Chinese artists and design-crossover projects.

galleries.name: Gallery Func
galleries.note: Design-conscious gallery pairing contemporary art with collectible design and craft, active at Shanghai's fairs.

galleries.name: Modern Art Base
galleries.note: Independent exhibition base linked to the ZiWU creative platform, hosting experimental exhibitions and photography projects.

galleries.name: Galerie Dumonteil
galleries.note: Paris/New York/Shanghai gallery specialising in modern and contemporary sculpture and animalier traditions; a durable Concession presence.

galleries.name: Matthew Liu Fine Arts
galleries.note: Dealer-run gallery with an internationalist programme spanning Chinese contemporary art and Western modern works on paper.

galleries.name: Basement 6 Collective
galleries.note: Artist-run underground collective known for experimental, performance and sound programming outside the commercial circuit.

galleries.name: Swatch Art Peace Hotel
galleries.note: Artist residency on the Bund with public exhibition galleries; an unusual long-term platform for international artists working in Shanghai.

galleries.name: Ren Space
galleries.note: Villa-based independent art space presenting cross-disciplinary exhibitions bridging traditional aesthetics and contemporary practice.

galleries.name: V Art Center
galleries.note: Nonprofit exhibition space at M50 supporting young artists and curatorial experiments.

galleries.name: Other Gallery
galleries.note: Shanghai space of the Beijing-founded gallery, with a programme of conceptual and installation-based Chinese artists.

galleries.name: FQ Projects
galleries.note: Small independent gallery focused on emerging Asian artists and intimate solo presentations.

galleries.name: AM Art Space
galleries.note: Compact Concession-edge gallery with a consistent programme of contemporary ink, photography and young Shanghai artists.
